column2: How do I record the casts of a bronze sculpture?
column3: The sculpture’s record → “🔥 Casts and editions” → “＋ Add a cast”. Each cast is a small record: engraved number (1/8, EA I…), founder, date, process (lost wax, sand), patina, patinator, foundry mark, weight, posthumous cast, “ours”, where it is and who owns it, provenance and sales, photos. The table of casts can be filtered (all, during the artist’s lifetime, posthumous); the planned edition (“8 + 4 EA”) recalls the legal limit. Enlargements, reductions and versions are linked at the bottom of the record.

column2: How do I follow a play, its productions and its tours?
column3: Create the play (author, genre, acts, characters, publication), then “＋ Add a production”: company, director, team, music, cast (character, performer, understudy). In each production: “＋ Add a performance” (date, town, venue, audience, première…) and “＋ Add a tour”. The play’s record shows everything as a Tree, a Table, a Calendar or on the Map.

column2: How do I create my own type of work (carnival float, carved clog…)?
column3: “＋ New work” → “＋ Create my own type…”. In 5 steps: 1 · name, plural, icon, family, start from scratch or from an existing type, “part” records (a float has editions); 2 · the fields, arranged in groups: 24 kinds (text, date, duration, dimensions, list of choices, person + role, place, linked record, image, table, calculation…), or taken from other types in the library; each field has its help, its starting value, “required”, “shown by default” and “in the search”; 3 · the possible links to other types, named in both directions; 4 · the columns of the list and the lines of the thumbnails; 5 · the preview. Your type has the same tools as the others; ⚙️ Manage the types → ⤓ to export it and give it away.

column2: Where is the list of craft trades, and how do I record a piece of ironwork?
column3: “＋ New work” → “Design and crafts” family → “⚒️ The 16 fields of the craft trades…”: the official French list (order of 24 December 2015), with search by trade or speciality. Choosing a trade opens the right type of work with the trade noted. A piece of ironwork: kind (gate, banister…), patron and decision, where it is installed, designer, metal, techniques (forged, riveted, repoussé…), dimensions, decoration, hallmark, workshop and journeymen, preparatory drawings, commission (quote, paid, deadlines), protection (Historic Monuments, Mérimée database), states and restorations.

column2: How do I note that a person was a craftsperson (apprenticeship, compagnonnage, MOF)?
column3: Tick the “🔨 Craftsperson” profile (or, in the craft trades window, “🔨 “Craftsperson” profile”). Their page gains its sections: 🧑‍🏭 Training and apprenticeship (master, contract, CAP diploma, schools), 🛠 Compagnonnage (guild, journeyman name, Tour de France, masterpiece), 🎖 Titles (Meilleur Ouvrier de France, Maître d’art, Entreprise du patrimoine vivant), 🏭 Workshop · business, 🔏 Hallmarks and marks, ⚒️ their pieces. “…” on a section to write it.

column2: How do I import a bibliography?
column3: Catalogue → 📚 Bibliography → ⤒ Import: Open Library by ISBN (on the back of the book), all the books by an author, or the books on a subject (they arrive under “About him / about her”), or Wikidata. Cover, publisher, year, pages, ISBN and language are filled in. Each book gives its link with the artist (by them, about them, illustrations, translation, preface, exhibition catalogue) and where to find it (library, shelfmark, at home).

column2: How do I show, hide or arrange the fields of an artist’s record (record, track, painting…)?
column3: On the record, “⚙️ Shown fields”: by groups (Release, Tracks and credits, My copy, Identifiers…), 👁 shows or hides a field, ⠿ (drag) or ↑ ↓ arranges it, and the form follows the same order. A hidden field keeps what is written in it; when reading, an empty field is never shown (“Hide empty fields” switch). Tabs: The record, The list (the columns), The thumbnails, The export (what goes into an entry and into the book). The setting applies to all artists, or only to this one (“Setting specific to…”). “💾 Saved settings”: save under a name, ⤓ export, ⤒ import; ↺ Reset to default.

column2: How do I add my own fields to a record, a work, a book?
column3: “⚙️ Shown fields” → “＋ Add a field” (or at the bottom of the form): a name (“Bought by”, “Listened to on”…) and its kind: text, long text, number, date, period, duration, dimensions, measure + unit, amount, list of choices, labels, yes/no, rating out of 5, web link, code, person, place, linked record, image · sound · video, document, colour, note. Tick “For all records…” to have it everywhere. Your fields go into “✎ My fields” (or the chosen group), can be renamed (✎) and removed (🗑, with “↶ Undo”; “Put back a removed field” brings them back).

column2: How do I create my own kind of record (sculpture, poster, carnival float…)?
column3: In the catalogue, “＋” at the end of the tabs → “＋ Create a kind of record…”: a name, the plural, an icon, a family, and “Start from…” nothing or an existing kind (its fields are taken over). Then “⚙️ Shown fields” to add, arrange and hide its fields. It has its list, its filters, its export, and its records link to others like the app’s kinds.

column2: How do I change or remove the emoji in front of a menu tab (🧬 DNA, 📒 Notes…)?
column3: Settings → Appearance → “Order and names of the main menu”: to the right of each tab, the small box contains its emoji. Type or paste another one ({mac:⌃⌘Space|pc:⊞ + .}), or empty the box to have none, then “Save”. “↺ Reset the names to default” also puts back the original emojis.

column2: I have the same record or the same book twice, three times: how do I note it?
column3: On its record, in “📦 My copy (collection)”: the first copy is described as usual (condition, storage, price, dedication); below, “Other copies (duplicate, triplicate…)” → “＋ One more copy” adds a line per copy, each with its condition, its edition or pressing, its place, its price, its value and its dedication. ⚙️ Shown fields lets you show or hide this line.

column2: How do I link a track to its takes, its mixes and the records it appears on?
column3: The track (🎵 the written work: lyrics, music, publisher, SACEM…) has its recordings: “＋ Add a recording” (take, mix, remaster, version, live), each with its date, studio, duration, sound file (▶), credits, “made from” (the mix of a take…) and “chosen take”. On a record, each track can point to a recording (purple badge): the track’s record then shows the tree of takes and mixes and, for each, the releases (record, track, format, year, duration). “Tree | Table” changes the view.

column2: How do I record the provenance, exhibitions and bibliography of a painting?
column3: On the work’s record: “Provenance” (one line per step: date, how — the artist, given, sold, bought back, inheritance… —, who, detail, price) reads like a timeline; “Exhibitions”: each exhibition is a record (🏛), with the catalogue number and the lender; “Bibliography of the work”: the book or article (📚 record) and the page. Also: catalogue raisonné and inventory numbers, where it is and who owns it, states and restorations, value and insurance, related works (study, sketch, replica, engraving after, pendant), editions and casts.

column2: How do I make the book of the catalogue raisonné or the discography?
column3: In the list of works (or records), “📖 Create the book…” — or Page layout → “🖼 Catalogue raisonné” / “💿 Discography”. Choose the artist, the design, the format, the works (those of the filtered list, or all), the order, the parts of the book (to tick and arrange: cover, introduction, chronology, entries, exhibitions, bibliography, index, concordances…), the fields of each entry and the layout (a double page per work, one, two or four per page). The book opens in the page layout; each entry follows the work’s record: File → “↻ Update the dynamic objects” picks up a corrected provenance.

column2: How do I organise an artist’s page?
column3: Catalogue → 🎨 Page → “⚙️ Organise the page”: each section (biography, artistic identity, awards, discography, works, exhibitions, bibliography, filmography, concerts…) can be arranged (⠿ or ↑ ↓), hidden (👁) and take the whole line, half or a third. “Template” starts from the discipline (Musician, Painter, Writer, Filmmaker, Photographer, Sculptor, Architect); “＋ Add a section” for your own (“Their instruments”…). A section’s “…” button edits the artist’s profile (stage names, bands and their members, labels, galleries, training, awards, official links, press).

column2: Why “Mentioned in artists’ catalogues” on a person’s record?
column3: A person chosen in a catalogue (credit on a record, owner of a painting, dedication, band member…) sees this block on their record: “Paris canaille (1958) — accordion”. The links read both ways: the record’s page also shows the person in “🔗 Linked to”. A name without a record (grey “?” badge) can become a record later.

column2: How do I record a concert or a show with its setlist (setlist.fm-style)?
column3: Artist’s catalogue → 🎤 Stage tab (or “＋” → 🎤 Stage and shows → Concerts and performances) → “＋ New concert or performance”. Choose the kind of evening (concert, comedy, theatre, dance, circus, orchestra, storytelling): the setlist adapts (songs, sketches, scenes, acts, works). Each line points to the record of the track, sketch or scene (“＋ Create” if it does not exist yet); 📝 on a line for the cover, the 👤 guests with their role, the dedication, the 1st or last time, a version, “unfinished”, the duration. “＋ An encore”, “📋 Paste a list” (one title per line), “📋 Copy another evening’s setlist”. The title fills itself in (“Joseph MARTIN in Tulle, 14 July 1958”). On the record, a title without a record has “＋ record” to create it in one click.

column2: How do I see the most played tracks, the first and last time, the map of concerts?
column3: 🎤 Stage tab: the top bar offers List, Cards, Map, Timeline and 📊 Statistics. The statistics (most played titles with the first and last time, evenings per year, country, town and venue, average length, titles per evening, typical setlist of a tour, never played live, compare two evenings, roles and understudies in the theatre, conductors and soloists, who goes on stage most often) are calculated on the filtered list: filter a tour, a town, years or a title played to see them change. On the map, the size of the marker = the number of evenings; a click shows the list for that place.

column2: How do I group the dates of a tour?
column3: On an evening’s record, “Tour” field → “＋ Create the record “…””. The tour’s record shows its dates (each evening shows “date 12/31”), the route on the map and the typical setlist (the title most often played in each position, encores included). “＋ Add a date” creates the next evening, already linked to the tour.
